body: Superseded by #443, which now targets `main` and carries this branch's commits (its head `4fa6698` is in that history). The BLS discussion stays here.

Added a second commit for 25.md: its bolt12 example quote is locked to the same pubkey (03d56ce4...), but the PostMintBolt12Request example had no signature, so per NUT-20 a mint would reject it (20008). It now uses the same example key as 20.md and carries a valid BIP340 signature over msg_to_sign for that quote id and those outputs.

> I reviewed d9928f06 while implementing Nutroot v3 in CDK #2951 (https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/2951).

Thanks @thesimplekid, that was a really useful pass. All eight changes are in d9ea05c through efaf0bd, vectors in cashubtc/cashu-ts#1508, the check example on main in #492.

For implementers syncing vectors: as at 10d8a69 the shared JSON (the NUT-10/28 worked examples, transcripts, tokens, the five-leaf fold and the NUT-29 duplicate-quote request) is cashubtc/cashu-ts@e82d6f819b761c4726f9c915dd6ad4d1439646ec `test/vectors/nutroot-v3.json`, from cashubtc/cashu-ts#1508. The spec copies it verbatim.
Closing: #422 redefines the check as best-effort and removes this section, so the fix belongs there.

Regarding @thesimplekid's [comment on NUT-13 type `0x04`](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/443#discussion_r4668792124): this does not belong in the minimal viable set of changes. Specifically, the new mint-identity-scoped HMAC derivation, per-mint quote counter, and deprecation of the existing NUT-20 BIP32 path should be split into a dedicated PR. Nutroot can use the existing quote-key derivation or random quote keys without these changes.

Nutroot can use the existing quote-key derivation or random quote keys without these changes.

NACK to removing the NUT-13 quote key derivation, for the reasons stated [in the reply to the comment](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/443#discussion_r4671947263) above.

Cross-checked with a second implementation: nutshell (`cashu` 0.21.0 from PyPI), calling its own `cashu.core.nuts.nut20.verify_mint_quote` on the examples as they stand in this branch:

- 20.md `PostMintBolt11Request`, pubkey `03084290...05e5`: **True**
- 25.md `PostMintBolt12Request`, same pubkey: **True**
- current main 20.md, pubkey `03d56ce4...7cac`: **False**, even with nutshell's legacy (pre-length-prefix) fallback

So the replacement pair verifies in nutshell and not only in my own code. The example key is `sha256("NUT-20 example quote key")` if anyone wants to re-sign. Expect different signature bytes because nutshell signs with random aux_rand; verification is the meaningful check.

Cross-checked with a second implementation: libsecp256k1 via coincurve (`PublicKey(bytes)` parse, which rejects points not on the curve), run over every compressed point in the three files. This branch: 11.md 0/6, 14.md 0/5, 29.md 0/6 invalid. Current main: 11.md 1/6 (`02e2aeb97f...`), 14.md 1/5 (same key), 29.md 2/6 (`0208657b29...`, `037dc0b5e7...`) invalid. So the replacements parse in libsecp256k1, not only in my own curve code.

@Egge21M forwarding from vnprc:

My use case: a mining pool mint where each accepted share becomes one NUT-20 locked mint quote. A miner's key can collect thousands of quotes a day, and the wallet polls the lookup to find the ones it hasn't minted yet.

The spec says quotes in every payment and issuance state are eligible and has no state filter. For me that means every poll pages through the whole history, almost all of it already issued, to find a handful of new ones. Cost per poll grows with the key's lifetime instead of with what's outstanding.

Request: an optional filter for quotes that still have something to mint (amount paid greater than amount issued), applied before the page limit so a full page of spent history can't hide mintable quotes behind it. I run this today as only_mintable on the #341-style lookup and it's what keeps polling cheap. A state field would work just as well if you'd rather generalise it.

Two smaller notes:

+1 to binding the payment method into the signed message. I filter by method for the same reason it's in the path.
The spec orders by quote ID. With a mintable-only filter, any stable order works for me.

Happy to share numbers or test against an implementation.
